standard_prerequisites.name: The Noetherian property of a topological space as the ascending-chain condition for open subsets (equivalently the descending-chain condition for closed subsets), and the induced topology on a subset
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on Noetherian topological spaces, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the property to be proved and the topology on the union.

core_obligations: Descending chains: the proof takes a descending sequence of closed subsets of the union with the induced topology (proof lines 1553-1554).
Lifting the chain to the ambient space: it produces a descending sequence of closed subsets of the ambient space whose intersections with the union recover the given sequence (proof lines 1555-1559).

Finiteness and the chain condition: using the finiteness of the index set, the proof applies the Noetherian property of each of the finitely many pieces to conclude that each of the finitely many relevant chains stabilizes, and hence so does the given chain (proof lines 1559-1566).
Conclusion: the union is Noetherian with the induced topology (proof lines 1566-1567).
proof_roadmap: 取并集（带诱导拓扑）中的闭集降链，把它提升为全空间中的闭集降链。
利用指标集有限，对有限多段分别用各 X_i 的 Noetherian 性，得到各段在有限步后稳定，从而原链稳定。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the stability of the Noetherian property under finite unions with the induced topology (author lemma at source lines 1544-1550, label lemma-finite-union-Noetherian). The proof (source lines 1552-1567) is a complete chain-condition argument: a descending chain of closed subsets of the union is lifted to the ambient space (proof lines 1555-1559), and the finiteness of the index set is then what allows the author to apply the Noetherian hypothesis on each piece and conclude that the lifted chain, and therefore the original one, stabilises (proof lines 1559-1566). The lemma is the companion of the result that images of Noetherian spaces are Noetherian, both being basic closure properties for the chapter's later constructibility results. H2.
